 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Placenta** is responsible for the **nutrition** of the fetus. It is an organ that develops in the uterus during pregnancy.
 
• The **fallopian tube** is the site where **fertilization** occurs. It connects the ovary to the uterus and is where the sperm meets the egg.
 
• The **uterus** is where the embryo **implants** and grows during pregnancy. It is a muscular organ located in the female pelvis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Placenta**__

 __
 
• The **placenta** provides oxygen and nutrients to the growing baby and removes waste products from the baby's blood.
 
• It attaches to the wall of the uterus, and the baby's umbilical cord arises from it.
 
• It acts as a protective barrier against certain infections and substances.
 
 
 
• **Fallopian Tube**__
 __
 
• The **fallopian tube** is also known as the oviduct or uterine tube.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the reproductive process by transporting the egg from the ovary to the uterus.
 
• Blockages or damage to the fallopian tube can lead to infertility or ectopic pregnancy.
 
 
 
• **Uterus**__
 
 
• The **uterus** is also known as the womb.
 
• During pregnancy, the uterus expands significantly to accommodate the growing fetus.
 
• After childbirth, the uterus contracts to help expel the placenta and minimize bleeding.
